title: Plan a Trip
text: Plan [a 3-day trip to Edinburgh for two adults on about £400]. Give a day-by-day plan mixing sights and downtime, with one rainy-day option.
about: Get a day-by-day trip plan, with a rainy-day option.
try: a weekend in Tenby with two children
four days in Lisbon on a budget
two days in Bath by train

title: Choosing Wine
text: I'm serving [roast lamb with rosemary]. Suggest three drinks to go with it: a red, a white and one alcohol-free. Explain why each works.
about: Find a drink to match tonight's dinner.

title: Dinner from the Fridge
text: I have [eggs, spinach, half an onion, cheddar and a tin of tomatoes]. Give me three dinner ideas with prep time and steps.
about: Get three dinner ideas from what's in your fridge.
try: what's left in your own fridge

upload.text: Or upload a photo of your fridge

title: What to Watch Next
text: I liked [Slow Horses and Line of Duty]. Suggest five similar titles and say why I'd like each.
about: Get five recommendations based on what you already love.

title: Make a Complaint
text: Draft a complaint to [my broadband provider about three engineer visits that never happened]. Say what happened, what I've tried and what I want. Firm but polite, under 200 words.
about: Get a firm, polite complaint written for you.
try: a courier about a parcel left in the rain
a shop about a faulty kettle
a train company about a cancelled service

title: Reality TV Voiceover
text: Write a one-minute reality TV voiceover narrating [the office fridge being cleared out] as high drama. Include one confessional-booth quote and end on a cliffhanger.
about: Get an ordinary moment narrated as high drama. Just for fun.
try: choosing where to go for the team lunch

title: What Could Copilot Do for My Job?
text: I'm [a team administrator]. Suggest five tasks Copilot could speed up, with an example prompt for each. Flag anything I shouldn't paste in.
about: Get five ways Copilot could help with your job.

title: This Could Have Been an Email
text: Turn this meeting agenda into an update email people can reply to by 5pm: [budget update, new rota, office move].
about: Turn a meeting agenda into an update email instead.
try: the agenda for your next team meeting

title: Fix My Prompt
text:
My prompt didn't give me what I wanted. Rewrite it so that it does. Give me the improved prompt first, then a short list of what you changed and why.
My prompt: [PASTE YOUR PROMPT]
What I got: [PASTE THE REPLY, OR DESCRIBE IT]
What I wanted: [DESCRIBE A GOOD ANSWER]
about: Paste your prompt, what you got and what you wanted. Get a better prompt back.
note: Test the new prompt in a new chat.

title: Plain-English Small Print
text: Put this clause into plain English: [The tenant shall indemnify the landlord against all claims arising from the tenant's use of the premises.] Tell me what I must do, what I can't do, and any risk.
about: Get a contract clause explained in plain English.
try: a clause from terms and conditions
a paragraph from a tenancy agreement
note: Good for understanding. It is not legal advice.

upload.text: Or upload a photo of the small print

title: How Do I Do That?
text: Give me step-by-step instructions to [set up an out-of-office reply in Outlook]. Name the exact menus and buttons, and suggest one shortcut.
about: Get step-by-step instructions for any app.
try: freeze the top row in Excel
schedule a Teams meeting for a group
note: Menus change. If a step doesn't match your screen, tell Copilot what you see.

title: Sort My To-Do List
text: I have these tasks: [finish the budget report, book the training room, reply to 40 emails, plan next year's away day]. Sort them into Do, Decide, Delegate or Delete, and say why.
about: Sort your tasks into do, decide, delegate or delete.
try: your own to-do list for this week

title: Ten Odd Ideas
text: Give me ten unconventional ideas to solve [low turnout at our staff events]. One sentence each, plus a first step.
about: Get ten unusual ideas for a problem, each with a first step.

title: Build a Tiny Web Page
text: Build a single-file web page that [counts down the days to my next holiday]. I'm not a developer: give me the complete code and tell me exactly how to open it.
about: Build a small working web page without knowing any code.
try: shows a random lunch idea when I click a button
works out how many days until Friday
note: Save the code as a file ending .html, then double-click it.

title: Why Is My Formula Broken?
text: My Excel formula gives an error: [=VLOOKUP(A2,Sheet2!A:B,3,FALSE) shows #REF!]. Explain why in plain English and give me the corrected formula.
about: Find out why a formula is failing and get it fixed.
try: a formula of your own and the error it shows

upload.text: Or upload a screen grab of the error

title: Made-Up Test Data
text: Make a table of 10 made-up [customers with a name, email, region and amount spent] for testing. Make them look realistic but clearly fake: use @example.com for any email.
about: Get realistic made-up data for testing.
try: library books with a title, author and due date
job applicants with a name, role and interview date
orders with a product, price and delivery date

title: Pull Details Out of a Mess
text: Pull the name, email and phone number of each person out of this text and put them in a table: [Hi, it's Sam Example here, you can get me on 029 2018 0123 or sam@example.com. My colleague Alex Sample is on alex@example.com.] Write "Not given" where something is missing.
about: Pull names, emails and phone numbers out of messy text.
try: made-up notes from a phone call
note: Practise with made-up details, not real people's.

title: Spot the Odd One Out
text: Flag anything that looks odd in this list and say why: [Expense claims: Train £42.50, Lunch £8.20, Train £42.50, Taxi £18, Lunch £820, Parking £6].
about: Find the entries in a list that don't look right.
try: a column of your own figures

upload.text: Or upload a spreadsheet of figures

title: Simplified Technical English
text:
Explain this [TOPIC/TEXT/DOCUMENT] at about 80% of the way to ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English.
Use short sentences. Use active voice. One idea per sentence.
Use simple, common words.
Explain technical terms the first time they appear.
Give steps in order, one action per step.
about: Get anything explained in short, simple, step-by-step English.

title: Write the Prompt for Me
text: I want Copilot to help me [write a monthly update for my team]. Write the best prompt for that. Include a role, the context you need from me and the format. Mark the gaps I need to fill in CAPITALS.
about: Say what you want and get Copilot to write the prompt.
note: Copy the prompt it writes into a new chat to use it.

title: Mark Your Own Work
text: Check [your last answer]. List anything that was guessed, anything that could be out of date, and the one thing I should verify myself. Then give me a corrected version.
about: Get Copilot to check an answer for guesses and out-of-date facts.
try: this answer (paste it into a new chat)
note: Run it in the same chat, then in a new chat with the answer pasted in. A new chat isn't anchored to its own words.

title: Socratic Tutor
text: Act as a Socratic tutor. I want to understand [how compound interest works]. Don't explain it or give me the answer. Ask me one question at a time, wait for my reply, and build on what I say. If I get stuck twice, give me a hint, not the answer. When I type DONE, tell me what I now understand and what to look at next.
about: Learn a topic by being asked questions, not told the answers. Type DONE when you've had enough.
try: how AI chatbots choose the next word
the difference between mean and median

title: Your Executive Coach
text: Act as an experienced executive coach. I want to work on [delegating more instead of doing everything myself]. Use the GROW model: my goal, where I am now, my options, and what I will do. Ask one question at a time and wait for my answer. Challenge vague answers, and don't give advice unless I ask for it. When I type WRAP UP, summarise my goal and my next three actions.
about: Get coached through a work challenge, one question at a time. Type WRAP UP to finish.
note: Keep it about you. Leave out colleagues' names and details.

title: Learn SQL on Your Own Tables
text: Act as a patient SQL tutor. Here is my table: [orders(order_id, customer_name, order_date, region, amount)]. Set me five practice questions on it, easiest first, one at a time. Wait for my query each time. Then say what is right, fix what is wrong, and explain the correct query clause by clause.
about: Practise SQL on your own table, with feedback on every query.
try: a CREATE TABLE statement of your own
note: Paste the column names only, never the data in the table.

title: Explore a Spreadsheet
text: I've uploaded [a spreadsheet of this year's training bookings]. First, list each column, what it holds, and any blanks or odd values. Then give me the three most useful findings, such as trends, outliers or gaps. For each one, say which columns you used and how you worked it out. Finish with three questions I should ask next.
about: Upload an Excel file and get its columns, key findings and next questions.
note: Remove names and personal details before you upload. Check its sums against the file.

title: Check My Spreadsheet
text: I've uploaded [a spreadsheet of expense claims]. Act as a careful data checker. Look for duplicates, blanks, typos, mixed formats (such as dates or numbers stored as text), totals that don't add up and values that look out of range. Give me a table: Problem, Where (sheet, column, row), Why it matters, Suggested fix. Don't change anything, and tell me if you couldn't read part of the file.
about: Upload an Excel file and get a list of errors to fix.
note: Remove personal details before you upload. Spot-check a few of the rows it flags.

title: Check My Work
text: Act as a careful reviewer. Check [the report I've uploaded] before I send it. Look for numbers or dates that don't agree with each other, claims with no evidence, missing steps and anything unclear. Give me a table: Issue, Where, Why it matters, Fix. Mark each one Must fix or Nice to fix. Don't rewrite it.
about: Get a piece of work checked for errors and gaps before you send it.

upload.text: Upload the document, or paste the text

note: Use a new chat: one that helped write the work goes easy on it. It still won't spot everything, so the final check is yours.

title: Themes in Free-Text Feedback
text: I've uploaded [an Excel file of comments from our staff survey]. Use Python code to read every comment in the free-text column, so the counts are real. Group the comments into themes. Give me a table: Theme, Number of comments, Typical quote. Then list the top three issues, the top three things people liked, and two insights I might miss. Tell me how many comments you read.
about: Upload feedback comments and get themes, issues, positives and insights, with counts.
note: Remove names and anything that identifies a person first. Check the counts against the file.
